newsitem.title: USA: More debt issues seen on tap for US corp bond mart.
newsitem.headline: More debt issues seen on tap for US corp bond mart.

text.p: Corporate bond issuance is expected to pour in at a steady rate as healthy demand by investors has another $2.0 billion in investment-grade debt on tap for this week, dealers said.
"There's still a lot of demand for corporate paper and several names are out there," said one high-grade syndicate source. "Deals continue to be well received."
Among upcoming issuers are Chrysler Corp's $600 million A3/A-minus rated 30-year debt offering via Salomon Brothers Inc.
Caterpillar Inc is among other names circulating in the market, sources said.
Caterpillar is expected to issue between $300 and $400 million in 100-year bonds, callable after fifty years, via lead underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co.
In addition, Seagate Technology Inc may also tap the market with a three-part Baa3/BBB rated $750 million debt offering via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, sources said.
The offering is expected to consist of a seven-year issue, 10-year issue, and a 40-year tranche with a put option in the twelfth year.
And Enterprise Rent-A-Car is gearing up to tap the corporate bond new issue market with a $250 million 144A private placement debt offering via Goldman Sachs & Co.
The deal is expected to consist of a seven-year issue, sources added.
As demand for paper continues to grow, boosted by investors' search for higher yield, a slew of junk issues are slated to hit the market as well.
ICG Communications is expected to set a $200 million two-part 144A debt offering via sole manager Morgan Stanley & Co.
Another $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes is expected to come to market out of of Fairchild Semiconductor Corp.
Quality Food Centers is also getting set to tap the market with $125 million in senior subordinated notes due 2007 via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
Roseburg Forest Products is also expected to issue $200 million in a four-part 144A debt offering.

The deal is expected to include the following issues: a seven-year issue with price talk at 105 basis points, 10-year with price talk at 115 basis points, 12-year with price talk at 120 basis points, and 15-year with price talk seen at 130 basis points, sources said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading off 10/32 at 99-16/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
